purpose: Full PR #173 comparison against C Oniguruma, plus opt-in cache document comparison and isolated process memory.
input_pins_toml:
# Canonical external input pins for the publishable `battle_bench` reference suite.
# Update this file whenever battle inputs or their source snapshots change.
format_version = 1

[oniguruma]
repo = "https://github.com/kkos/oniguruma"
commit = "f95747b462de672b6f8dbdeb478245ddf061ca53"
local_cache_dir = ".cache/upstream/oniguruma-orig"
prepare_script = "scripts/prepare-oniguruma-sources.sh"

[scanner_wrapper]
file = "benches/vscode_scanner_native.c"
source_repo = "https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-oniguruma"
source_path = "src/onig.cc"
imported_in_ferroni_commit = "ad96196d0f883dec0a552d359fa2f8f37d299962"
sha256 = "74e57ca90d0251932837195e0dbaf9194327c8b8c62f13a654a22cdec587c479"
note = "Locally extracted C scanner wrapper used by battle_bench."

[grammars]
source_repo = "https://github.com/shikijs/textmate-grammars-themes"
imported_in_ferroni_commit = "0e7016172a4563d385b362bca15308cc6225449f"
note = "Full committed grammar snapshots consumed by benches/grammar_loader.rs."

[[grammar]]
id = "typescript"
file = "benches/grammars/typescript.json"
sha256 = "e86e45f551919f50ac5e5cf89990c3520877305b35708294de5ae83c9b6ca559"

[[grammar]]
id = "css"
file = "benches/grammars/css.json"
sha256 = "eeed15521cc9e32ef9a92fa36dbf3674a6c13ba2fc20c666ef8c257e355246ec"

[[grammar]]
id = "rust"
file = "benches/grammars/rust.json"
sha256 = "41ad4b92eff153b69b65d03216d2f787861d3a23a0b4ab7a3ee8d6d6c016e34f"

[memory_workload]
scenario = "typescript_scanner_large"
kind = "deterministic synthetic TypeScript source"
repeat_blocks = 16000
driver = "line-by-line first-match scanning with full committed TypeScript grammar"
template_revision = 3

criterion_configuration.note: Each group sets these values. Criterion may extend slow cases to collect 30 samples; raw sample times are retained. Point estimates use slope where present, otherwise mean; confidence intervals are 95%.

commands.pr173-css-repeat: cargo bench --locked --features ffi --bench battle_bench -- scanner_documents/css_117 --noplot --save-baseline pr173-css-repeat
commands.pr173-cache-documents: cargo bench --locked --features ffi,match-cache --bench battle_bench -- scanner_documents --noplot --save-baseline pr173-cache-documents
commands.memory: ./scripts/run-battle-memory.sh (three sequential runs; one engine per process; default Ferroni features)

method_notes: The reference run compiles match-cache out. The second run compares runtime cache off/on in the same feature-enabled executable against C.
Timed single-pattern and text searches request no capture output from either Ferroni or C. Untimed checks compare match positions and raw capture bounds.
Scanner preflight checks compare token indices and every capture range against C before timing; fixture inputs are ASCII.
Warm scanner cases reuse one subject; existing per-string memoization differs from the C wrapper below 1000 bytes. Document cases reset identity per line.
A factor is C time divided by Ferroni time, not a confidence interval or a cross-workload aggregate.
Memory is process high-water RSS, not isolated engine allocations or opt-in cache usage. The driver takes the first match per line, not a full token trace.
All measurements ran sequentially on a developer workstation; fixed engine order and one machine limit generalization.
